title: Ultimate
tagline: One Android app of small offline tools: video editing, shrinking, audio extraction, a sound meter and an app inspector. No ads, no accounts, no internet permission.
stateNote: The README describes a large, active toolkit. I haven't built or installed the app, so what it does comes from the README.
problem: Phone utilities are usually cluttered with ads and trackers, and each one is a separate app. Ultimate keeps small tools in one place, and the standard edition's manifest has no INTERNET permission, so it cannot reach the network.
audience: Android users who want simple tools that stay on the phone, and anyone curious how apps track them.
contribution: It is my project. It brings together my earlier standalone Android tools (Squeeze and Pluck) into one codebase that can also be built as separate apps.
worksToday: Studio: an offline video editor with a timeline, trim and split, speed, titles, music and H.264/AAC export, per the README.
Squeeze: shrinks videos with the phone's hardware encoders, with size targets and a before-and-after player.
Video to audio: extracts MP3, M4A or WAV from a video.
Sound meter: live microphone levels with sessions and CSV export, and no audio recorded.
Pluck: lists installed apps, extracts their APKs, and scans for ad and tracker SDKs offline.
One codebase builds several editions (Ultimate, Squeeze, Pluck and others). The latest commit mentions a terminal and SSH/SFTP work.
limitations: I haven't built or run it. Everything here comes from the README and commit history.
A separate Traffic Inspector edition needs the internet permission. The README says its relay hasn't been run against a real phone's VPN tunnel in the repository.
No download or store link that I can verify.

involve.headline: Want to try a build, or have a tool in mind?
asks: If you're an Android user, tell me which small offline tool you wish existed.
If you do Android or Kotlin work, I'd welcome a second pair of eyes on the architecture.

disclosure.note: Public repository. This page is written from its README and the public build.

approach: Started as separate standalone Android tools (Squeeze and Pluck), then merged them into one codebase where each tool is a plug-in.

Every tool implements one small interface (a screen, a library of what it made, and how to remove it), so Home, the Library, the Activity tab and share routing pick up a new tool with no other changes.
One foreground service and one notification cover long-running work for every tool, each with its own cancel action and a live log of the decisions it made.
Product flavors build the same code as six different apps, from the all-in-one Ultimate to single-tool editions, each with its own app id and icon.

decisions.why: The standard edition's manifest never asks for INTERNET, so privacy is enforced by Android rather than promised. The traffic inspector, which needs the network, ships only as separate editions.
Each edition switches tools on with constants, so the build strips every tool an edition doesn't include instead of hiding it at runtime.
The tracker scanner describes what each ad SDK typically collects and why apps include it, as general descriptions rather than claims about one app's configuration.
